title: Metroid Ravenous Logo Memes Make Phrases Like “Girl Dinner” And “They Took My Ass” Look So Metal
description: Hype emanating from the reveal of Metroid Ravenous has translated into an onslaught of memes after a logo generator circulated online. If you're on Reddit or Bluesky, you may have seen the instantly iconic image of Samus Aran aggressively pinning down a mysterious enemy for consumption, but now accompanied by stupid text like "I ASKED FOR NO PICKLES" in the Metroid Ravenous font. The Pixelframe Design website unveiled a tool that lets anyone input any text and style it to look like the grainy and jagged Metroid Ravenous logo, with four options for the image background. Pixelframe Design previously made similar logo generators for games like GTA 6, The Duskbloods, and famously, Pokopia. https://bsky.app/profile/pixelframe.bsky.social/post/3mvlab7xqde2o The apparent hook of Metroid Ravenous is Samus's need to kill and consume her enemies to survive. Naturally, that has led to food-related memes like a riff on the "55 burgers" scene from I Think You Should Leave, a reference to the viral concept of "girl dinner," or a simple but effective "Om Nom Nom" joke. Literally any wording you put into the generator will look more badass in this font. https://www.reddit.com/r/Metroid/comments/1whfq4q/hungry_samus_thats_it_thats_the_joke/ It's also been amusing to see other video game titles like Hello Kitty Island Adventure in the Ravenous font face, and several other of these memes are just vulgar and gross enough to be hilarious. Don't expect any of this to become official Nintendo marketing material. https://bsky.app/profile/gusbod.bsky.social/post/3mvlioodyv22v The Metroid subreddit was briefly jam-packed with these images, leading to moderators creating a megathread devoted to the meme template. Hilariously, many of the top-upvoted comments are Ravenous memes dunking on the mods. Revealed during the September 2026 Nintendo Direct, Metroid Ravenous is a follow-up to 2021's Metroid Dread and a return to the 2D track of the franchise. While Nintendo hasn't officially commented on who is developing Ravenous, Dread studio MercurySteam hinted that it's behind the upcoming title on social media. Metroid Ravenous releases on January 28, 2027, and a special edition coming with a steelbook and Amiibo figure will also come out.

title: Resident Evil Director Was In Horrible Pain Making The Movie
description: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has revealed he was going through hell while making the movie, which is about a man going through hell. He told The Hollywood Reporter that he had pneumonia for the first half of filming on Resident Evil. For the second half of production, he had Campylobacter jejuni. This causes diarrhea, and man, that sucks for anyone, but especially if you're trying to film a big-budget, highly anticipated film based on a property with legions of fans and great expectations creatively and commercially. "So I was very, very ill for the whole production, and everything felt so barely in control because my body was failing me," Cregger explained. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mNd1gb19A-c Cregger said he credits his "wonderful, talented" department leads to help him through, while he also praised Resident Evil star Austin Abrams for going above and beyond. He said Abrams is "one of the most can-do, positive people I’ve ever met. I was spoiled by the people around me." Not only was Cregger physically sick while making Resident Evil, he had to deal with freezing-cold conditions in the north of the Czech Republic where the movie was filmed. "We froze our asses off," he said. This wasn't the first time Cregger was dealing with physical turmoil while making a movie. On his last film, Weapons, it was so hot and humid that he needed an IV and directed scenes remotely. Resident Evil releases on September 18, and it's expected to have a huge, record-setting opening weekend. The movie stars Austin Abrams as a medical courier named Bryan who is an "idiot" everyman who finds himself in a world of pain.

title: Resident Evil Is Now The Highest-Rated Gaming Movie Ever
description: The Resident Evil movie from Weapons and Barbarian director Zach Cregger releases in theaters on September 18. Reviews from critics went live today, and the movie is earning high scores. GameSpot's Resident Evil review scored it an 8 and said it successfully captures the breathless terror of the games. In fact, it's now the highest-rated video game movie ever. It boasts a mightily impressive 96% on Rotten Tomatoes from 71 reviews and an equally impressive 80 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic. According to Metacritic, Resident Evil is the highest-rated video game movie ever, well ahead of another 2026 movie, Exit 8, which has a 71 Metascore. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mNd1gb19A-c The six Resident Evil movies that Paul W.S. Anderson made did not score very high with critics, with 2016's The Final Chapter topping them all at 49% on Metacritic. The latest Resident Evil movie before Cregger's, 2021's Welcome to Raccoon City from director Johannes Roberts, scored a 44% on Metacritic. After that movie came out, Constantin, which has owned the movie rights to Resident Evil since the '90s, intended to put the franchise on hiatus. However, Cregger, coming off the success of Barbarian, pitched Constantin on his new, original take, and Constantin loved it so much that they put it into production. Video game movies had a track record of mediocrity at best for years, but the tide is turning in recent times. This could be for many different reasons, but some have theorized that part of what made video game movies of yesteryear poor in terms of reception was that, in large part, the game studios and creative minds behind them were not involved in the development process. That's changed now. Oliver Berben, the CEO of Constantin, said that while his team didn't contractually need to consult with Capcom, the film studio did so anyway to ensure it was respecting and caring for the IP and its fans. That might be a surprise to some gamers, as many have voiced their concerns and dislike for Cregger's take on Resident Evil, in part because he's telling a new story and not adapting any previous games or featuring any of its characters. Cregger said in press interviews that he felt like he was on an apology tour instead of a press tour due to the fan blowback. He's also admitted that he was naive to think fans would embrace him and his ideas, but ultimately he made the movie he wanted to, and it's clearly resonating with critics. Nintendo, meanwhile, went further than many have in terms of Hollywood adaptations. The company was not only creatively involved in The Super Mario Bros. Movie and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, but co-financed them. For 2027's The Legend of Zelda movie, Nintendo is putting up more than 50% of the funding, so it would seemingly get to call the shots. This contrasts with the arrangement Take-Two and Gearbox had for the poorly received and commercial flop that was the Borderlands movie. Lionsgate funded it, not Gearbox or owner Take-Two, and it was the film company that paid the price for the flop, at least financially. Resident Evil officially releases on September 18, but screenings begin on September 17. The movie is expected to have the biggest opening weekend ever for a Resident Evil movie. The film stars Austin Abrams, who had a standout performance in Cregger's Weapons, as a medical courier who takes on a job that brings him to Raccoon City. Everything goes badly, of course, and Abrams himself nearly died for real making the movie.

title: Lego Batman: Legacy Of The Dark Knight Gives Harley Quinn An Arkham Asylum Makeover
description: Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight was a fun tribute to the Caped Crusader when it launched earlier this year, but if you're tired of saving Gotham, you can embrace chaos with two of the city's greatest villains: Harley Quinn and the Joker. The duo are headlining the game's Mayhem Collection expansion, and just like Batman, they're dressing in style with multiple outfits that you can unlock during their caper. GameSpot can exclusively reveal one of them: a classic costume for Harley Quinn, pulled directly from 2009's Batman: Arkham Asylum. And still one of Harley's best outfits.While Harley Quinn predominantly wore a jester's outfit throughout her appearances in Batman: The Animated Series and related comic books, Rocksteady's Arkham Asylum game saw her switch up her look dramatically for what can best be described as a doctor-themed dominatrix. Out with the spandex onesie, in with a repurposed doctor's outfit, leather corset, domino mask, and other elements that paid homage to her roots. In Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, this costume is described as having prankster pigtails and a "chaotic" corset. https://www.youtube.com/shorts/2Gu8dw37ri4?feature=share In case you missed it, the Mayhem Collection draws heavily from Batman: The Animated Series, with developer TT Games calling the expansion a love letter to the landmark '90s show that introduced Harley Quinn as the Joker's sidekick. Fans can find several references to the series in the Mayhem Collection, along with Easter eggs for other Batman shows, films, games, and comic book stories. There's even a nod to Harley Quinn's original voice actor, the late Arleen Sorkin, and the new story mission chronicles the first meeting between the Joker and Quinn, back when she was still the ambitious psychiatrist Dr. Harleen Quinzel. The Mayhem Collection launches on September 18 for Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, one of the best games of 2026. It's also coming to Switch 2 on the same day, and it's also available for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S.

Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave’s Fantastic Reviews Have Me Feeling FOMO
description: Here we go again: A new Fire Emblem game is garnering glowing reviews, and I'm thinking this could be the one that finally clicks with me. Launching tomorrow on Switch 2, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave sits at a fantastic 89 metascore (at the time of publication) on GameSpot's sister site Metacritic. That's good enough to place it No. 13 currently on Metacritic's list for best games of 2026. In addition, GameSpot's Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave review says this is "the new high point to beat for future entries." As someone who didn't plan to buy the strategy RPG, I'm now second-guessing myself. I have a history of buying well-reviewed Fire Emblem games, trying them out for maybe five hours, and then bouncing off them for something else. That was especially true of Fire Emblem: Three Houses on Switch in 2019. Before that, my first foray into the series came in 2013 with Fire Emblem Awakening on the Nintendo 3DS, if you don’t consider me maining Marth in Super Smash Bros. Melee. This is a game I still have downloaded on my 3DS XL, which sits in the drawer of my bedside table. I've tried so many times to engage with the game, only to stop after a couple of hours. Once again, I don't dislike the turn-based action, but for some reason, it never fully connects. I'm obviously in the minority, because Fire Emblem Awakening basically saved the entire series. Those previous encounters with the Fire Emblem franchise had me ignoring Fortune's Weave, until now. I see the high praise for the Switch 2 exclusive and feel like I might be missing out on an amazing game. Sure, I'm currently in the middle of playing Blasphemous and have Final Fantasy 7 Remake waiting for me after picking it up on sale. But what if Fortune's Weave is the Fire Emblem game that finally, finally resonates with me? Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave launches tomorrow, September 17, on Switch 2. 28 Best Nintendo Switch 2 Games To Play Right Now View Images

title: Call Of Duty: Black Ops Dev Teases “Something That Nobody’s Ever Experienced Before”
description: Veteran Call of Duty developer Treyarch is finishing up its work on Black Ops 7 and shifting to its next project, but what will that be? That remains to be seen, but Treyarch design director Kevin Drew said in a new Dev Talk video that it might not be what you expect. Drew said Treyarch has "learned a lot" working on 2024's Black Ops 6 and 2025's Black Ops 7 and "tried a lot of things in our current era." "But we're ready to make something new and something that nobody's ever experienced before," he said. That sounds hyperbolic and extreme, and Call of Duty studios are definitely known for grandiose claims. Treyarch created the Black Ops series, which debuted in 2010, and it remains one of the most popular brands within the franchise. In an unusual move, back-to-back Black Ops games came out in 2024 and 2025, and Treyarch itself admitted it did worry about franchise fatigue. EA's Battlefield 6 outsold Black Ops 7 in 2025, with Black Ops 7 falling down to the No. 5 spot for the year, at least in the US. In another big shakeup for Call of Duty, and seemingly in a bid to sell more units, Microsoft announced that Call of Duty games will no longer be included with Xbox Game Pass at launch, beginning with this year's Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Infinity Ward is leading development on Modern Warfare 4, though, as usual, Activision's network of Call of Duty studios, including Treyarch, are expected to contribute to the game's overall development. An interesting rumor making the rounds related to Call of Duty claims that Microsoft--which owns Call of Duty and Activision--is considering having a Call of Duty studio work on a Halo game. Another rumor said Microsoft could "put Halo under Activision" as part of a larger restructuring to help Halo regain its prominence in the FPS market.

title: Fable Being “Vital To The DNA” Of Xbox Helped Shield The Game From Hardship, Director Says
description: The Fable reboot in development at Playground Games has been in the works for a long, long time, and part of what's "protected" the game during the lengthy development cycle was that the franchise is so closely associated with Xbox. That's according to Fable game director Ralph Fulton, who told The Guardian, "I genuinely think Fable is an important game." "What has protected us over a long development cycle is that so many people within Xbox view Fable as vital to the DNA of the platform,” Fulton said. “I would go a step further and say it’s important to video games as a whole. It offers a combination of elements that simply doesn’t exist anywhere else.” https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eUMgrbdTOLc While Fable may have been "protected," other Xbox games and studios cannot say the same. Throughout Fable's development period, Xbox shuttered studios, canceled games, and laid off staff. The latest round of cuts came this year, with Microsoft trimming 1,600 jobs, with another 1,600 layoffs still to come. Another dormant Xbox franchise, Perfect Dark, attempted its own reboot, but Microsoft canceled the game and shuttered its developer. Microsoft acquired Playground in 2018. The studio worked on Forza Horizon racing games exclusively, and Fable is the studio's first non-Forza game. Playground created a second team internally to work on Fable, and Fulton said, "Building a team from scratch is the hardest thing you can do in video games." Playground is taking over for Lionhead, which previously developed the Fable games until Microsoft shuttered the studio in 2016. The main series has been dormant since 2010's Fable 3, so fans have been waiting a long time for a new one. Also in the interview, Fulton teased the ending to Fable's story, saying it "really challenges you to think about who you are, with a real personal cost to weigh against the outcome." He said Playground "relentlessly pursed quality" for the game's ending, despite industry metrics that suggest only a relatively small percentage of people who start a game actually finish it. The Fable reboot was originally scheduled to release this year, but was delayed to February 2027. Fulton said the delay to 2027 helps avoid a "chaotic" window, and that's for sure a reference to staying out of the blast zone of GTA 6.

title: Bloodborne May Not Be Getting A Sequel Or Remaster, But How About An Umbrella?
description: It never rains, but it does pour for Bloodborne fans holding out hope for some news on From Software's beloved game. Fortunately, you can take some shelter from that storm of disappointment with an official Bloodborne umbrella, and a few items for anyone wanting some souls-like couture in their wardrobe. Announced by the SuperGroupies fashion label, the Bloodborne collection includes an umbrella, necktie & tie clip set, card holder, laptop sleeve, and book cover. The "Childhood's Beginning" umbrella features illustrations of the Caryll Runes on the exterior and a silhouette of the Moon Presence floating in front of the red moon over a field of white flowers on the interior. Even though it's the most pointless piece of clothing ever designed, if you really need a necktie, you can get the Lady Maria-inspired tie and gaze at patterns inspired by the fan-favorite hunter. The matching tie clip is modeled after the lumenflower brooch from her cravat. For the Bloodborne accessories, you can round out your look with a book cover that reflects the Vileblood Register, a card holder embossed with Caryll Runes, and a laptop sleeve that features a flap shape and studs that subtly reference the iconic Hunter Hat. Preorders start on September 15, and these items are expected to ship out in mid-April 2027. Here's a breakdown of how much they'll cost: Childhood's Beginning Model Umbrella -- $126 Lady Maria of the Astral Clocktower Model Necktie & Tie Clip Set -- $126 Vileblood Register Model Book Cover -- $96 Hunter Model Card Holder -- $136 Hunter Model Laptop Sleeve -- $156 While a Bloodborne remaster or sequel still looks unlikely for now--and could be for strategic reasons on Sony's part--fans can look forward to an "R-rated" animated feature in the future. YouTuber and gamer Seán McLoughlin, who goes by the name JackSepticEye, is on board as a producer, and he says he's approaching this film as a passion project that faithfully replicates the cult-classic game. As for From Software, the developer has been busy throughout the 2020s with its Elden Ring series, expansions, and spin-offs. Its next release is a Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods, a PvPvE multiplayer action game that has no confirmed release date yet but is still expected to launch in 2026.

title: Resident Evil Director On Who Should Play Lady Dimitrescu In A Resident Evil Village Movie
description: Director Zach Cregger's latest movie, Resident Evil, hits theaters this week, but if there were to be a movie based on Resident Evil Village, who should play the game's popular Lady Dimitrescu character? That's the question that Pedestrian TV put to Cregger recently. He said his choice would be Christina Hendricks. "That feels about right to me," he explained. Lady Dimitrescu, a tall vampire woman, was one of the most popular characters in Village. She was based on Morticia Addams and other wicked women. The developers at Capcom have spoken about her design, saying they wanted to avoid making her look too much like a Gothic vampire. Hendricks is best known for playing Joan on AMC's Mad Men, for which she received multiple Primetime Emmy nominations. Hendricks is also known for playing Beth in NBC's Good Girls. She is an accomplished voice actor, too, having portrayed Gabby Gabby in Toy Story 4 and Cherie in Solar Opposites. Lady Dimitrescu.Hendricks has one video game credit to her name, and that's the role of Sam Harper in 2011's Need for Speed: The Run. In Resident Evil Village, Lady Dimitrescu is portrayed by Maggie Robertson. She won the Best Performance award at The Game Awards for her performance. It remains to be seen if Lady Dimitrescu could be featured in a movie one day, but the latest Resident Evil movie comes to theaters this Friday, September 18. The film does not feature any characters from the games, though there will be Easter Eggs and nods to the series for fans to obsess over, co-writer Shay Hatten said.

title: Blizzard Boss On Why Diablo Is Becoming A TV Show And How Involved The Studio Will Be
description: At BlizzCon, Blizzard announced a partnership with Netflix for an animated Diablo TV show. The announcement caught some by surprise, but Blizzard president Johanna Faries said in an interview that it makes sense for the studio because many people simply don't have the time to invest meaningfully in Blizzard's games, but still might watch a Diablo TV show. “We have so much fandom around Blizzard that doesn’t always necessarily translate into hardcore gaming time,” she told The Los Angeles Times. “This is another way to deepen the relationship with our Diablo community and expand and broaden the conversation with our fans and potentially attract new fans, who may not have the time ... to be able to devote hours to the gameplay, but certainly can devote hours to being engaged in this new form of storytelling." Faries went on to say that Blizzard will be "very involved" with the Diablo show. This isn't always the case for transmedia adaptations, as Naughty Dog recently confirmed it will have no creative involvement in The Last of Us Season 3 on HBO. Additionally, Larian is not involved in the upcoming Baldur's Gate show. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M1Tpajd58o8 Lydia Bottegoni, the executive vice president of story and franchise development at Blizzard, said bringing Diablo to Netflix part of an effort aimed at "meeting people where they are." "The franchises themselves and the characters in the worlds have a lot of depth and a lot that we can share," Bottegoni said. It is still early days for the Diablo TV show, and there is no word yet on the story, cast, or release date. It won't be the first Blizzard property to be adapted in Hollywood, as Blizzard and Legendary worked together on the 2016 Warcraft movie. It made just $47 million in the US, but brought in $225.5 million from China alone, finishing with more than $400 million globally. Plans were prepared for sequels, but the domestic box office being so poor contributed to why those never materialized. As for the Diablo game series, Blizzard just recently announced Diablo 5, but it's not coming for some time.
